summary: Tested Binance Token Scanner backend + frontend end-to-end. 22/23 backend tests pass. All 15 timeframes return 200 with valid data; /api/tokens sorting/search/bad-timeframe/detail/status all correct. Frontend renders white dashboard with 671 USDT pairs, timeframe pills, virtualized table, search filter, sort dropdown, 1s auto-refresh confirmed (footer Σ trades ticked 131→184 over 3s). Only issue: /api/market-overview CoinGecko fields (totalMarketCap, totalVolume24h, btcDominance, activeCryptos) are null because CoinGecko public API returns HTTP 429 rate-limit from this server IP without an API key.

minor.issue: CoinGecko returns 429 (rate limit) with no API key set — resulting in totalMarketCap/totalVolume24h/btcDominance/activeCryptos = null. Sources reports 'coingecko: error: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' because response body on 429 sometimes contains empty text. Backend should either (a) parse the 429 error message from JSON (it IS JSON) and surface it clearly as 'rate limited', or (b) instruct user to add COINGECKO_API_KEY. Frontend then shows '--' for Total Mkt Cap / 24h Volume / Active Coins in the overview strip.

integration_issues.issue: Total Mkt Cap, 24H Volume, Active Coins render '--' due to upstream CoinGecko 429 (no API key). Not a frontend bug but a UX consequence.

action_items: Set COINGECKO_API_KEY in backend/.env (demo key from coingecko.com) to unblock totalMarketCap/btcDominance/activeCryptos. Alternatively add graceful retry/backoff or fallback to another provider.
In server.py market_overview cg(): check r.status_code before r.json() and surface 'rate limited' message clearly instead of the confusing JSON parse error.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py market_overview functions call r.json() without checking r.status_code first — masks HTTP error causes (currently seen on CoinGecko 429).
poll_binance loop uses broad `except Exception` — fine, but consider also catching cancellation properly. Overall code quality is good and file is under 400 lines.
Frontend Scanner.jsx uses two intervals + control-change effect — small chance of duplicated fetch bursts, but functionally acceptable.
seed_data_creation: None — engine warms up from live Binance polling.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py and parametrize over all 15 timeframes. CoinGecko rate-limit is the only real gap; adding an API key or a graceful fallback will make the market_overview test pass fully. Data source is data-api.binance.vision (api.binance.com is geo-blocked). Engine warms up in ~2s; long-timeframe approx=true is expected before enough history accumulates.
